Is Nvidia the Central Bank of AI?

Every dollar Nvidia has put behind the companies that buy its chips, with sources.

This register finds 80 financial relationships in which Nvidia has put money, credit or demand behind companies in the AI buildout, and every number on this page links to its source.

Of the amounts that can be confirmed, $30.2 billion is invested and still held, $37.7 billion is committed, and $107.4 billion is contingent on events such as a tenant's default.

$105 billion of the contingent amount is a guaranty of OpenAI's rent that is signed but not yet in force.

Announcements add up to $307.1 billion, which is never counted as exposure; $103.5 billion of it is letters of intent or deals with no disclosed agreement.

Nvidia's own accounts show more than any outsider can name: it paid $58.1 billion for equity in the nine months to 25 October 2026, and this register can tie $10.5 billion of that to named deals.

Funded, committed and contingent add up to gross exposure of at least $175.3 billion. It is a lower bound: 50 of 80 relationships have a part that is not disclosed. Click a tile to filter.

Guaranties of OpenAI's PORTS-Pike leases from SB Energy, capped at $105 billion

Nvidia guarantees OpenAI's lease value at an Ohio campus up to $105 billion once buildings are ready, so it pays exactly when OpenAI cannot.

FundedNot applicable
CommittedNot applicable
Contingent maximum$105 billionas of 25 October 2026 not yet in force Source (6)
Headline$105 billionas of 17 August 2026 Source (2)

Announced 17 August 2026 · Signed 17 August 2026 · Not yet in force · Matures Not disclosed · Last verified 23 November 2026

Significance82 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

On 2026-08-17 Nvidia entered into residual value guaranties with SB Energy, the lessor, covering about 4.25 GW of IT load leased for 20 years to an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC at the PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio. Nvidia pays only if OpenAI's tenant defaults (insolvency or an uncured monetary default); each guaranty takes effect when its building is ready for service, the first expected in Nvidia's fiscal 2029, and the guaranteed amount declines as OpenAI pays rent. The aggregate cap is $105 billion; the guaranties end on OpenAI reaching a designated credit rating, at lease end, or after 20 years, and OpenAI must reimburse Nvidia. The tenant is VELA I Holdings, LLC, whose parent OpenAI Global, LLC guarantees its obligations by joinder; OpenAI's non-payment is the trigger, so the exposure is recorded against OpenAI, and SB Energy's building subsidiaries are the beneficiaries.

Seniority: Guarantor

Both sides

Result: Partly reconciled

What Nvidia disclosed. 8-K and 10-Q: guaranties capped at $105 billion for about 4.25 GW, nine phases, first effective in fiscal 2029, triggered by tenant default, exposure declines as OpenAI pays, terminates on a satisfactory OpenAI credit rating, OpenAI reimburses Nvidia, option on about 3.8 GW more (ev_30001, ev_30009, ev_10040, ev_120001, ev_120002, ev_120005, ev_30007, ev_30008, ev_30004). No payments made to date (ev_30023). Source (7)

What OpenAI disclosed. OpenAI: secures about 8 GW-IT; 20-year lease; NVIDIA provides credit support for the initial 4.25 IT-GW; rent starts only as completed capacity is delivered (ev_120022, ev_120025, ev_120024, ev_120023). SB Energy S-1/A: aggregate guaranteed value and remedy cap of $105 billion on the initial 4.25 GW-IT; trigger is tenant insolvency or an uncured monetary default; OpenAI compensates NVIDIA under a separate agreement; 17 leases for about 8.0 GW-IT commencing 2028 to 2032 (ev_40089, ev_40090, ev_40091, ev_40094, ev_40098, ev_40099). Source (10)

  • optional additional capacity: Nvidia side about 3.8 GW (8-K, 10-Q); 3.75 IT-GW (press release); counterparty side remaining 3.78 GW-IT (SB Energy S-1/A) Source (3)
  • compensation for the guaranty: Nvidia side Site exclusivity for NVIDIA infrastructure given in exchange (10-Q); counterparty side Compensation provided separately by OpenAI under a separate agreement, amount not disclosed (SB Energy) Source (2)
  • if Nvidia declines the option: Nvidia side Not addressed; counterparty side OpenAI must secure a replacement guarantor rated at least A- (SB Energy) Source

Credit read
Wrong-way risk
Specific: exposure grows as the counterparty weakens. Nvidia pays only when OpenAI cannot pay rent, so the exposure is drawn exactly as OpenAI's credit fails; SB Energy states OpenAI is not an investment-grade tenant.
Collateral
No security for Nvidia. The landlord must pursue the tenant parent concurrently (ev_100050) and Nvidia looks solely to the tenant and tenant parent for recoupment (ev_100003). On a trigger Nvidia may assume the tenancy, have the landlord re-let, or sell (ev_40096); recovery depends on reletting a campus purpose-built for Nvidia infrastructure. OpenAI's reimbursement and indemnity is an unsecured claim on the defaulted tenant (ev_30008, ev_120007).
Tenor
Over 10 years: up to 20 years per building from each lease commencement, leases commencing 2028 to 2032; no guaranty is in force before the first building is ready, expected in Nvidia's fiscal 2029.
Cash and undrawn facilities
$4.7 billion (at least), 31 March 2026 Source
GPU collateral
No GPU-backed debt of OpenAI itself found in allowed sources. Compute is mostly contracted from clouds and lessors (Microsoft, AWS, CoreWeave, Oracle, SB Energy).

First order consequences

Analysis

  • If OpenAI's tenant becomes insolvent or misses rent at PORTS-Pike, Nvidia pays SB Energy the shortfall and can recover only from OpenAI's tenant entities under their reimbursement promise. Source (3)
  • If OpenAI Group PBC reaches a credit rating designated in the guaranty, whose level is not disclosed, Nvidia is released, so its exposure depends on OpenAI's credit path. Source
  • Because each guaranty takes effect only when its building is complete, Nvidia's exposure to OpenAI keeps rising through construction even if OpenAI's finances weaken meanwhile (analysis). Source (2)
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Lender relianceSB Energy says PORTS-Pike's financeability depends in significant part on the Nvidia guaranty, so future project lenders would be underwriting Nvidia's credit as much as OpenAI's; no project debt exists yet. Source (2)
  • Collateral loopOn an OpenAI default Nvidia may assume or re-let the lease, and the campus may host only Nvidia infrastructure, which tests what that capacity is worth without OpenAI. Source (2)
  • ContagionPORTS-Pike makes up most of SB Energy's backlog, so OpenAI's credit drives SB Energy and its controlling shareholder SoftBank as well as Nvidia. Source
Timeline
  • 17 August 2026: Nvidia signs residual value guaranties with SB Energy for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike leases, capped at $105 billion. Source (2)
  • 17 November 2026: Nvidia reports maximum exposure of $105.0 billion to the SB Energy guarantees and no payments to date. Source (2)
  • 19 November 2026: SB Energy's S-1/A describes the guaranty trigger, remedy cap and OpenAI's non-investment grade status. Source (2)
Research notes

Executed Building 1 guaranty and form: see research/reports/R5_cluster_de.md, Guaranty terms (ev_100001 to ev_100051): tenant VELA I Holdings, LLC (ev_100008), tenant parent OpenAI Global, LLC (ev_100009), letter agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC (ev_100010), guaranteed minimum value constant then declining (ev_100014), no covered project debt in place yet (ev_100020). Coordinate with the vehicle cluster (SB Energy). Nvidia's separate $3.0 billion equity in SB Energy belongs to that cluster. Seniority recorded as guarantor. Dates: signed and filed 2026-08-17; effective left null because no guaranty is in force until the first building is ready for service, expected in fiscal 2029 (ev_120002, ev_30027); maturity left null because it differs per building (up to 20 years from each lease commencement). Tier 2 history: late July 2026 reports of talks on a backstop of up to $250 billion were cut to the signed $105 billion cap (needs quote, see R5 report). Critic round 1: contingent_max marked not in force (in_force false) with the date the first guaranty can take effect; effective and maturity stay null because no source gives a calendar date for either.

First order consequences

Analysis

  • A lower OpenAI round price would lead Nvidia to mark down its OpenAI stake, as it already records impairments on private stakes it holds (analysis). Source
  • OpenAI says its training fleet and most inference run on Nvidia GPUs, so the money Nvidia put into OpenAI supports demand for Nvidia's own systems. Source
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • SignalingSoftBank paid its $30 billion in three tranches beside Nvidia's OpenAI commitment, so a pause by Nvidia in OpenAI's next round would be read first by the same co-investors. Source (2)
  • ContagionOpenAI has contracted about $250 billion of Azure services, $38 billion of AWS compute and up to about $18.4 billion of CoreWeave capacity, so stress at OpenAI would hit Nvidia's stake and those cloud contracts together. Source (4)

Significance44 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Nvidia bought 214,776,632 newly issued Intel common shares at $23.28 each for $5.0 billion in cash under a securities purchase agreement signed on 15 September 2025. The sale closed on 26 December 2025 after the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period. The stake came with a collaboration under which Intel builds Nvidia-custom x86 CPUs and x86 SOCs with Nvidia RTX GPU chiplets. Nvidia's 13F shows 161,082,488 shares at 30 September 2026.

Seniority: Common equity

Both sides

Result: Reconciled

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia's release (2025-09-18) says it will invest $5 billion at $23.28 per share subject to regulatory approvals; its Q3 FY2026 10-Q lists $5 billion in Intel within investment commitments subject to regulatory approval; its FY2026 10-K reports gains on the Intel stock; its 13F reports 214,776,632 shares at 2025-12-31 and 161,082,488 at 2026-09-30. Source (11)

What Intel disclosed. Intel's 8-K (2025-09-18) reports the agreement of 2025-09-15 for 214,776,632 shares at $23.28 for $5.0 billion, subject to HSR, with no governance or information rights; its 8-K (2025-12-29) reports closing on 2025-12-26; its 10-K and Q3 2026 10-Q repeat the terms (215 million shares, rounded). Analysis

Analysis

  • SignalingNvidia buying SB Energy stock at 90% of the IPO price lends support to the offering, which a withdrawal by Nvidia would remove (analysis). Source (2)

First order consequences

Analysis

  • If CoreWeave cannot refinance its 2027 maturities, Nvidia's common stake sits behind about $47.5 billion of principal and could lose most of its value. Source (2)
  • A fall in CoreWeave's share price flows straight into Nvidia's other income, because the stake is held at fair value. Source (2)
  • CoreWeave's at-the-market program and convertible notes can dilute Nvidia's share of the company without any decision by Nvidia. Source (3)
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • SignalingGalaxy Digital's investor presentation for notes on its Helios campus leased to CoreWeave cites Nvidia's stake of about 11.5% and its capacity order, so an Nvidia sale would remove a support those noteholders were told about. Source (2)
  • ContagionA CoreWeave failure would strand capacity contracted by Microsoft, OpenAI and Meta and remove a buyer that runs only Nvidia GPUs. Source (5)
  • Collateral loopEnforcement on CoreWeave's GPU-backed loans would put used Nvidia GPUs on the market and lower the collateral values other lenders rely on. Source (2)

Nvidia convertible loan notes in Nscale (2028 Convertible Loan Notes and the NVIDIA Sale)

Nvidia has lent Nscale $1 billion in notes that convert into shares at the IPO, so its claim becomes junior equity as project debt grows.

Funded$1 billionas of 15 September 2026 Source

Contingent maximumNot applicable
Headline$2 billionas of 12 November 2026 Source

Announced Not disclosed · Signed 15 September 2026 · Effective 15 September 2026 · Matures 15 June 2028 · Last verified 23 November 2026

Significance53 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Under a subscription agreement of 15 September 2026 Nvidia subscribed for $1.0 billion of Nscale's unsecured 2028 Convertible Loan Notes and agreed to a further $1.0 billion, the NVIDIA Sale, settled in notes or non-voting shares and due to close on or around 16 November 2026. The notes accrue interest at 2% rising to 5.5%, mature on 15 June 2028 and convert automatically into non-voting shares at the IPO. They are recorded apart from the preferred shares because they are debt until converted.

Seniority: Unsecured creditor

Both sides

Result: One side only

What Nvidia disclosed. No Nvidia disclosure naming Nscale or these notes found as of 2026-11-23.

What Nscale disclosed. Nscale's S-1/A states $1.0 billion of the notes was subscribed by Nvidia and a further $1.0 billion will be issued to Nvidia in the NVIDIA Sale; the subsequent events note says $2.0 billion of the $3.1 billion programme is with Nvidia (ev_40011, ev_40012, ev_80019). Source (5)

General: moves with the AI cycle. A fixed loan amount; the exposure does not grow as Nscale weakens, but recovery falls with it, and both move with AI demand.

First order consequences

Analysis

  • If the Nscale IPO fails, Nvidia holds unsecured notes due June 2028 that rank behind GPU-backed lenders, at interest rising to 5.5%. Source (2)
  • If the Nscale IPO completes, Nvidia's notes convert into non-voting shares, so a creditor claim becomes equity priced by the IPO. Source
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Lender relianceNscale's secured lenders, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, sit above $2 billion of Nvidia notes, so Nvidia money absorbs Nscale losses before theirs (analysis). Source (2)
  • Collateral loopNscale's $24 billion of equipment commitments are largely Nvidia GPUs, so Nvidia's note money helps buy the hardware that secures Nscale's other lenders (analysis). Source (2)
Timeline
  • 15 September 2026: Nvidia subscribes for $1.0 billion of Nscale convertible loan notes and agrees a further $1.0 billion NVIDIA Sale. Source (2)
Research notes

Classification: FC with EQ secondary. The notes are unsecured debt until the IPO and become non-voting equity on conversion; recorded separately from the preferred shares because ranking and tenor differ.

Significance40 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Under a securities purchase agreement of 11 March 2026 Nebius sold Nvidia a pre-funded warrant over 21,065,936 Class A shares for gross proceeds of $2.0 billion. The exercise price is $0.0001 per share, so the warrant carries the full economics of the shares. Nvidia agreed not to sell for six months, to 11 September 2026.

Seniority: Warrants

Both sides

Result: Reconciled

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia's release says it will invest $2 billion in Nebius (ev_30052); its Schedule 13G reports 21,065,936 shares issuable on exercise of a pre-funded warrant acquired 2026-03-11 (ev_40053, ev_40051). Source (3)

What Nebius disclosed. Nebius reports gross proceeds of $2,000 million for the pre-funded warrant at $0.0001 exercise price (ev_40055, ev_40056) and describes the agreement in its 20-F (ev_40057). Source (4)

First order consequences

Analysis

  • Because the exercise price is nominal, Nvidia's Nebius warrant loses value exactly as Nebius shares do, so Nvidia carries full equity risk on the $2 billion. Source
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Revenue qualityNebius relies on Nvidia for its GPUs, so part of Nvidia's $2 billion may come back as Nvidia revenue; Nebius does not disclose its Nvidia purchases (analysis). Source
  • SignalingNebius raised a term loan, $5.75 billion of convertible notes and a Citi facility after Nvidia invested, so an Nvidia sale would weaken a signal its later lenders may have relied on (analysis). Source (3)
  • ContagionMicrosoft and Meta have contracted Nebius capacity of up to $17.4 billion and $27 billion, so a Nebius funding failure would hit Nvidia's warrant and those customers' capacity together. Source (2)
Timeline
  • 11 March 2026: Nvidia and Nebius sign the securities purchase agreement and Nvidia pays $2.0 billion for a pre-funded warrant. Source (3)
  • 20 July 2026: Nvidia files a Schedule 13G reporting 22,256,412 Nebius shares, 9.3% of Class A, including the warrant shares. Source (2)
Research notes

Seed B6 confirmed and extended: besides the 13F common stake, Nvidia invested $2.0bn through a pre-funded warrant. No Nvidia capacity purchase, backstop or guarantee for Nebius was found.

Significance40 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

On 31 March 2026 Nvidia bought 2,000,000 shares of Marvell Series A convertible preferred stock for $2.0 billion in cash, signed and closed the same day. Each share has a $1,000 stated value and converts at about $91.84, into at most 21,778,000 common shares, at Nvidia's option once the HSR waiting period ends. The preferred has no redemption rights and shares pro rata with common stock in a liquidation. Marvell provides custom XPUs and scale-up networking compatible with Nvidia NVLink Fusion.

Significance66 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Under a Guarantee of Lease Agreement of 14 October 2025, Nvidia guarantees Nscale's payment obligations under a net lease of a facility in Ward County, Texas, for the first five years of the lease. In return Nscale issued Nvidia warrants over Series B preferred shares, plus default warrants that become exercisable only if Nscale defaults on the lease. Nscale holds an escrow as recourse for Nvidia.

Seniority: Guarantor

Both sides

Result: Partly reconciled

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-10-26 reports one facility lease guarantee, maximum gross exposure $860 million, given in exchange for warrants, with $470 million placed in escrow by the partner (ev_10159, ev_50074, ev_10160). Nvidia does not name the partner. Matching amount, escrow, warrant consideration and quarter identify it as Nscale (analysis). The guarantee is now one of the land, power and shell guarantees totalling $3.5 billion (ev_10123). Nvidia never names Nscale, the landlord or the site. Source (4)

What Nscale disclosed. Nscale's S-1/A of 2026-11-12 states Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $860,340,000 of its obligations under the Ward County lease for the first five years, against a $470.0 million escrow and Series B warrants (ev_40003, ev_40046, ev_40004, ev_40006, ev_40007). The landlord Ionic Digital's S-1/A states Nscale provided a guarantee from NVIDIA Corporation for the lease (ev_170012), a third party confirmation of existence but not Nvidia's side. Source (6)

  • mitigants: Nvidia side Escrow $470 million; partner executed an agreement to sell the data center cloud capacity; counterparty side Escrow $470.0 million; no capacity sale agreement mentioned in the guarantee disclosure Source (3)
  • guarantor's own disclosure: Nvidia side Nvidia does not state the beneficiary, landlord, site or lease; the link to Nscale rests on matching amount, escrow, warrants and quarter (analysis); counterparty side Nscale and its landlord Ionic Digital both name NVIDIA Corporation as guarantor of the Ward County lease Source (3)

Wrong-way risk
Specific: exposure grows as the counterparty weakens. Nvidia pays only if Nscale defaults on the lease, so the exposure turns into a payment exactly when Nscale is weakest. The default warrants then give Nvidia more Nscale equity, which is worth least at that moment.
Collateral
$470.0 million escrow held by Nscale as restricted cash as recourse for Nvidia during the guarantee period (ev_40004). Default warrants over Series B preferred shares exercisable on a Relevant Default Event, fair value $11.3 million at issue (ev_40007). Nvidia may also look to the warrant shares, but their value depends on Nscale.

First order consequences

Analysis

  • If Nscale misses rent on the Ward County lease, Nvidia pays the landlord up to the cap and recovers first from the $470.0 million Nscale escrow. Source (2)
  • A Nscale lease default also makes Nvidia's default warrants exercisable, turning part of a guarantee loss into a larger Nscale stake worth least at that point. Source
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Lender relianceJPMorgan and Goldman Sachs fund GPUs in Nscale's Ward County building, so Nvidia's lease guarantee keeps their collateral housed even if Nscale stops paying rent (analysis). Source (2)
  • SignalingNvidia's credit let Nscale sign a large Texas lease while it relied on financing not yet committed, so without such guarantees Nscale would need cash deposits instead. Source (3)
  • Lender relianceIonic Digital, the Ward County landlord, has about $1.95 billion of contracted rent over the initial term, and Nvidia's guarantee covers the first five lease years, so Ionic's financing of the site looks to Nvidia's credit before Nscale's (analysis). Source (2)
Timeline
  • 14 October 2025: Nvidia signs the Guarantee of Lease Agreement for Nscale's Ward County, Texas facility and receives Series B warrants. Source (2)
  • 19 November 2025: Nvidia's 10-Q reports its first facility lease guarantee, $860 million maximum, with a $470 million partner escrow, without naming the partner. Source (2)

Significance31 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

In September 2025 Nvidia and OpenAI signed a letter of intent under which Nvidia intends to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI progressively as each gigawatt of Nvidia systems is deployed, alongside OpenAI deploying at least 10 GW. Both sides said details were still to be finalized. No definitive agreement for this structure has been disclosed by either side as of 2026-11-23; in February 2026 Nvidia instead committed equity to OpenAI's funding round, recorded separately.

Seniority: None

Both sides

Result: Partly reconciled

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia release: intends to invest up to $100 billion progressively (ev_30021). Q3 FY26 10-Q: a letter of intent with an opportunity to invest in OpenAI (ev_10156). FY26 10-K (2026-02-25): finalizing an investment and partnership agreement (ev_10125). Q1 and Q2 FY27 10-Qs do not name OpenAI as an investee. Source (3)

What OpenAI disclosed. OpenAI release of the same date: NVIDIA intends to invest up to $100 billion progressively (ev_120020), details to be finalized (ev_120021). OpenAI has published nothing since that converts the letter of intent into a definitive agreement; its February 2026 round release describes a separate $30 billion investment. Source (2)

  • current status: Nvidia side 10-K of 2026-02-25 says an agreement was being finalized; later 10-Qs silent; counterparty side No statement since September 2025 Source (2)

First order consequences

Analysis

  • The letter of intent ties Nvidia's investment to each gigawatt OpenAI deploys; if OpenAI keeps deploying Nvidia systems without a signed agreement, Nvidia gains the sales without investing (analysis). Source (2)
  • If Nvidia and OpenAI signed the letter's terms, investment released progressively as each gigawatt is deployed would become a commitment tied to OpenAI's own purchases of Nvidia systems (analysis). Source (2)
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • SignalingOpenAI and Nvidia said only that they look forward to finalizing the details, so lessors and clouds serving OpenAI cannot count the letter's headline as funding for OpenAI (analysis). Source (2)

First order consequences

Analysis

  • SpaceX's AI segment carries billions of dollars of GPU lease payments to Valor, so weaker returns at SpaceXSI would lower the value of Nvidia's SpaceX shares through other income (analysis). Source (3)

Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Lender relianceAnthropic can cancel SpaceXAI capacity on ninety days notice from early 2027, while SpaceX keeps paying Valor for the GPUs it leased. Source (3)
  • Collateral loopValor and the Apollo-managed lessor own the AI hardware leased to SpaceX, so a faster Nvidia product cycle would cut the collateral value behind SpaceX's leases (analysis). Source (2)

CoreWeave, Inc.

Capacity backstop Definitive Filed Neoclouds Specific wrong-way risk

Nvidia order for CoreWeave's residual unsold capacity

Nvidia must buy the capacity CoreWeave cannot sell through 2032, so its payments rise as demand weakens, until an insolvency ends the order.

FundedNot disclosed
CommittedNot disclosed
Contingent maximumNot disclosed
Headline$6.3 billionas of 9 September 2025 Source

Announced 15 September 2025 · Signed 9 September 2025 · Effective 9 September 2025 · Matures 13 April 2032 · Last verified 23 November 2026

Significance57 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

On 9 September 2025 Nvidia placed an order form under its master services agreement with CoreWeave with an initial value of $6.3 billion. CoreWeave sells reserved capacity to its own customers first, and Nvidia is obligated to purchase the residual unsold capacity through 13 April 2032, subject to CoreWeave meeting delivery and availability of service requirements. Either party may terminate on an uncured breach or an insolvency proceeding not dismissed within 90 days.

Seniority: Buyer of last resort

Both sides

Result: One side only

What Nvidia disclosed. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23. No Nvidia filing or release names CoreWeave's residual capacity order. Nvidia reports only unnamed aggregates: multi-year cloud service agreements of $26 billion at 2025-10-26 (ev_10151) and, from Q2 FY2027, AI cloud agreements of $36 billion that the AI clouds can stop providing and sell to third parties (ev_10035, ev_10039). Whether this order sits in either aggregate is not stated.

What CoreWeave disclosed. CoreWeave's 8-K of 2025-09-15, restated in its 424B3 of 2025-09-26, discloses the order form with an initial value of $6.3 billion and NVIDIA's obligation to purchase residual unsold capacity through 2032-04-13. CoreWeave's later 10-Qs and 10-K do not mention the order. Source (8)

  • existence and value: Nvidia side Not named; possibly inside the $26 billion cloud service agreement aggregate at 2025-10-26 (analysis); counterparty side $6.3 billion initial value Source (2)
  • label: Nvidia side Nvidia's own term for the closest category is AI cloud agreements, capacity the clouds can sell to third parties; counterparty side CoreWeave calls it access to residual unsold capacity; neither side uses the word backstop Source (2)
  • remaining performance obligations: Nvidia side Not applicable; counterparty side Not stated whether the order is in RPO. RPO language on committed capacity the Company has the right to resell first appears in the Q3 2025 10-Q, the quarter of the order (analysis) Source (3)
Credit read
Wrong-way risk
Specific: exposure grows as the counterparty weakens. Nvidia pays for whatever reserved capacity CoreWeave fails to sell, so its payments grow as CoreWeave loses customers while it remains solvent. The growth stops at failure: either party may terminate if the other's insolvency proceeding is not dismissed within 90 days, and on termination Nvidia is released from payment for services after termination. Payment also depends on CoreWeave meeting delivery and availability requirements, so a CoreWeave that cannot deliver is not paid. Analysis: US bankruptcy law can limit termination clauses triggered by a filing, so how far the 90 day clause protects Nvidia in a Chapter 11 needs legal review.
Collateral
None. Nvidia receives compute capacity for its payments; no security interest.
Tenor
2025-09-09 to 2032-04-13, about six and a half years.

GPU collateral
All GPUs in the fleet are NVIDIA GPUs (ev_20127) and customers contractually specify them (ev_20128). Computing equipment is depreciated over six years, changed from five in 2023 (ev_20130). Delayed draw term loans sit in special purpose vehicles that hold the financed infrastructure and the customer contracts (ev_20087); they are sized on the depreciable cost of GPU servers (ev_20144). SPV debt was secured by $22.2 billion of non-current assets at 2026-09-30 (ev_20086). DDTL 3.0 tracks collateral GPU by GPU using serial-number documents from NVIDIA or Dell (ev_20210). Latest generation deployed: Vera Rubin NVL72 (ev_20183).

First order consequences

Analysis

  • If CoreWeave's customers take less capacity, Nvidia pays for the unsold remainder, turning a weak quarter at CoreWeave into an expense for Nvidia. Source (2)
  • If a CoreWeave insolvency case runs past 90 days, Nvidia can end the order, so the purchase support disappears when CoreWeave most needs it. Source (2)
  • Delivery delays at CoreWeave reduce what Nvidia must buy, so the order protects demand risk but not construction risk. Source (2)
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Revenue qualityPayments for CoreWeave's unsold capacity return to Nvidia as GPU orders, so part of Nvidia's reported demand would rest on its own cash (analysis). Source (2)
  • Lender relianceLenders to CoreWeave may treat the Nvidia order as a demand floor, but it terminates on insolvency and is pledged in none of the credit agreements read. Source (3)
  • SignalingNew CoreWeave capacity without an Nvidia purchase floor would be priced on its customers alone, raising CoreWeave's cost of capital (analysis). Source (2)
  • Lender relianceA landlord's noteholders were shown the CoreWeave order as up to $6.3 billion of residual purchases, while the order ends after a 90 day insolvency, so those noteholders rely on support that stops when CoreWeave fails. Source (2)
Timeline
  • 9 September 2025: Nvidia signs an order form with an initial value of $6.3 billion to purchase CoreWeave's residual unsold capacity through 13 April 2032. Source (3)
  • 15 September 2025: CoreWeave files an 8-K disclosing the Nvidia order and its insolvency termination terms. Source (2)
  • 31 December 2025: CoreWeave amends DDTL 3.0 for delivery delays, cutting minimum liquidity to $100 million and postponing the coverage test. Source (4)
  • 31 March 2026: CoreWeave signs the $8.5 billion non-recourse DDTL 4.0 with MUFG as agent; no Nvidia agreement is pledged. Source (2)
  • 18 May 2026: CoreWeave signs the $3.1 billion DDTL 5.0 with Morgan Stanley as agent, backed by two non-investment grade customers. Source (2)
  • 10 August 2026: CoreWeave signs the $2.6 billion DDTL 5.5 with JPMorgan as agent, backed by five redacted customer contracts. Source (2)

nvidia_paid is blank because MSA payments are not split between this order and other order forms. covered_project_debt is blank: no document ties any CoreWeave facility to the capacity this order covers. stress_inputs are not filled: the contracted floor, contracted and merchant shares and capacity value per quarter are not disclosed by either side. Seed B2 confirmed with modifications: the filing says initial value, not a fixed amount, and the order is conditional on delivery and availability requirements. Critic round 1: contingent_max set to unknown because the only primary source calls $6.3 billion the order's initial value; a landlord's presentation calling it up to $6.3 billion is a third party's description (ev_170016).

CoreWeave, Inc.

Capacity rental Definitive Filed Neoclouds

Nvidia rents compute from CoreWeave under a master services agreement

Nvidia rents compute from CoreWeave, which runs only Nvidia GPUs, so its rent helps pay for the chips it sold.

FundedNot disclosed
CommittedNot disclosed
Contingent maximumNot applicable
HeadlineNot disclosed

Announced Not disclosed · Signed 10 April 2023 · Effective 10 April 2023 · Matures Not disclosed · Last verified 23 November 2026

Significance47 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Under a master services agreement dated 10 April 2023, CoreWeave provides NVIDIA infrastructure and platform services through order forms that NVIDIA submits. CoreWeave reports that NVIDIA paid about $320 million to the end of 2024, $326.3 million in 2025 and $59.6 million in the first quarter of 2026. The values and terms of individual order forms are not disclosed.

Seniority: Renter

Both sides

Result: One side only

What Nvidia disclosed. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23. Nvidia names no counterparty for its multi-year cloud service agreements ($26 billion at 2025-10-26, ev_10151; $27 billion at 2026-01-25 by year, ev_10120). Nvidia's filings state no related-party transactions.

What CoreWeave disclosed. CoreWeave discloses the MSA with NVIDIA dated 2023-04-10 as a related-party transaction and a material contract, and the payments: about $320 million cumulative to 2024-12-31, $326.3 million in 2025 and $59.6 million in Q1 2026. Source (7)

  • related party status: Nvidia side No related-party transactions disclosed by Nvidia; counterparty side CoreWeave's proxy treats NVIDIA as a related party; its Q3 2026 10-Q related-party note does not list NVIDIA Source (2)
  • contract value: Nvidia side Not named within cloud service agreement aggregates; counterparty side Payments only; order form values not disclosed Source (2)
Credit read
Wrong-way risk
General: moves with the AI cycle. Nvidia is the renter. It can lose only prepaid rent, none of which is disclosed, and the cost of capacity it does not use. The exposure does not grow as CoreWeave weakens; both sides move with AI demand.
Collateral
None.
Tenor
Runs until all order forms expire; order form terms not disclosed.

GPU collateral
All GPUs in the fleet are NVIDIA GPUs (ev_20127) and customers contractually specify them (ev_20128). Computing equipment is depreciated over six years, changed from five in 2023 (ev_20130). Delayed draw term loans sit in special purpose vehicles that hold the financed infrastructure and the customer contracts (ev_20087); they are sized on the depreciable cost of GPU servers (ev_20144). SPV debt was secured by $22.2 billion of non-current assets at 2026-09-30 (ev_20086). DDTL 3.0 tracks collateral GPU by GPU using serial-number documents from NVIDIA or Dell (ev_20210). Latest generation deployed: Vera Rubin NVL72 (ev_20183).

First order consequences

Analysis

  • If Nvidia stops ordering, CoreWeave loses a customer that paid it $326.3 million in 2025, about 6% of revenue (analysis). Source (2)
  • A CoreWeave insolvency lets Nvidia end the agreement, but Nvidia would need to find the research compute elsewhere. Source (2)
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Revenue qualityNvidia's $705.9 million of rent to CoreWeave since 2023 sits beside CoreWeave's Nvidia GPU purchases, a round trip shown side by side, not netted. Source (4)
  • Collateral loopCoreWeave's lenders identify their GPU collateral from Nvidia documents, tying Nvidia's records to the security of CoreWeave's loans. Source

  • 10 April 2023: CoreWeave and Nvidia sign the master services agreement under which Nvidia rents CoreWeave capacity. Source (2)
  • 25 September 2025: CoreWeave files the Nvidia master services agreement as an exhibit to its S-4/A. Source (2)

Nvidia Master Cloud Services Agreement with SharonAI: reserved capacity with minimum revenue and revenue share

Nvidia carries minimum revenue on SharonAI capacity that outside buyers do not take, so its payments grow when those sales weaken.

FundedNot disclosed
CommittedNot disclosed
Contingent maximumNot disclosed
Headline$4.88 billionas of 12 June 2026 Source

Announced 12 June 2026 · Signed 8 June 2026 · Matures Not disclosed · Last verified 23 November 2026

Significance50 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Under a Master Cloud Services Agreement and Order Form 1 dated 8 June 2026, SharonAI reserves GPU capacity for Nvidia for six years, delivered in five phases. Nvidia will have little or no use of the capacity unless SharonAI cannot sell it to third parties; minimum revenue provisions apply, subject to third-party utilisation, and Nvidia earns a share of cloud revenue on capacity sold. SharonAI describes the structure as a revenue-sharing and credit-support model.

Seniority: Buyer of last resort

Both sides

Result: One side only

What Nvidia disclosed. No Nvidia disclosure of this agreement found as of 2026-11-23. Nvidia's 9 September 2026 Australia release names Sharon AI as a partner expanding land, power and shell capacity, with no agreement terms (ev_80029, ev_80028). Nvidia's aggregate neocloud agreements, whose commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing, may include it (ev_30090; analysis).

What SharonAI disclosed. SharonAI's 8-K and 10-Q describe the six-year agreement, the up to $4.88 billion contract value, minimum revenue provisions subject to third-party utilisation, Nvidia's limited use of the capacity, and notice obligations to Nvidia on capacity sold (ev_40143, ev_40144, ev_40145, ev_40146, ev_40148, ev_40149). First order consequences

Analysis

  • If SharonAI sells little of the reserved GB300 capacity to outside customers, Nvidia pays the minimum revenue on it, so a GPU customer becomes a cost for Nvidia. Source (2)
  • A SharonAI insolvency lets either side end the agreement, which would stop Nvidia's minimum payments but leave SharonAI's hardware commitments unfunded. Source
Second order consequences

Analysis

  • Lender relianceSharonAI committed about $4 billion of hardware for the Nvidia agreement and says it needs more financing, so lenders to those GPUs would look to Nvidia's minimum revenue (analysis). Source (2)
  • Revenue qualityNvidia earns product revenue on the GPUs SharonAI buys and underwrites SharonAI's rent on them, so part of that GPU revenue rests on Nvidia's own promise. Source (2)
  • ContagionNEXTDC leased SharonAI 72 MW, the same size as the Nvidia collaboration site, so a SharonAI failure would leave NEXTDC with empty capacity (site match is analysis). Source (2)
Timeline
  • 8 June 2026: SharonAI and Nvidia sign the Master Cloud Services Agreement and Order Form 1. Source
  • 12 June 2026: SharonAI announces the six-year Nvidia collaboration with a contract value of up to $4.88 billion. Source (2)
  • 16 November 2026: SharonAI's 10-Q says the Nvidia arrangement has minimum revenue provisions but no fixed aggregate contractual value. Source (2)

Classification: BK with LB secondary. The 10-Q calls Nvidia a customer, but Nvidia uses the capacity only when third parties do not and pays minimum revenue, which is a capacity backstop. stress_inputs are empty: the contracted floor, merchant share and rate are not disclosed.

Significance55 of 100 why Analysis
What the deal is

Firmus announced a strategic compute partnership with NVIDIA running through 2034, anchored by a 360 MW NVIDIA DSX campus in Batam, Indonesia, covering up to 170,000 NVIDIA accelerators. Firmus procures NVIDIA infrastructure through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model: NVIDIA earns product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity. Nvidia's own blog names Firmus as one of the first partners in this model. Neither side discloses the size or trigger of the credit support.

Seniority: Buyer of last resort

Both sides

Result: Partly reconciled

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia's blog of 2026-07-01 describes a revenue-sharing and credit-support model for AI clouds and names Firmus and its Batam campus (360 MW, up to 170,000 GPUs). Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-07-26 reports AI cloud agreements in aggregate ($36 billion) without naming partners. Source (5)

What Firmus disclosed. Firmus release of 2026-06-28: partnership through 2034, revenue-sharing and credit-support model, up to 170,000 accelerators, expected US$25 to 30 billion from committed offtake over six years. Source (5)

What the deal is

Nvidia's stakes in listed companies, measured at fair value, totalled the disclosed Level 1 and Level 2 amounts at 25 October 2026. Level 2 holds unregistered warrants and preferred stock convertible into common stock, which Nvidia's holdings report (Form 13F) does not list, and that report is dated 30 September 2026. Because the dates and the instruments differ, no unattributed remainder is computed; two bridge rows compare listed shares and Level 2 instruments separately.

What the deal is

Neoclouds buy Nvidia systems and Nvidia commits to rent the resulting capacity for about six years; the neocloud sells the capacity to others first and Nvidia uses or pays for what is left. The commitments take effect only if the neocloud finances the purchase and Nvidia accepts the capacity. No named agreement has a disclosed Nvidia maximum; SharonAI (headline up to $4.88 billion) and Firmus are named but not quantified, so the whole disclosed maximum is shown as unattributed.

Seniority: Buyer of last resort

Both sides

Result: One side only

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it. Source (3)

What Unattributed disclosed. No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

Specific: exposure grows as the counterparty weakens. Nvidia's payments grow when neoclouds fail to sell capacity to third parties, which is when those neoclouds are weakest.

What the deal is

Nvidia has signed data center leases with terms of up to twenty years that have not yet started, expected to commence between the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2033. Nvidia says it may assign some of these leases to third parties, so it has signed long leases on its own credit for capacity that others may use. Neither the landlords nor the third parties are named, so the whole amount is shown as unattributed.

Seniority: Renter

Both sides

Result: One side only

What Nvidia disclosed. Nvidia discloses the total in Exhibit 99.2 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 and says it may assign some of these leases to third parties; it names no landlord or assignee. Source (4)

What Unattributed disclosed. No landlord or assignee disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

Credit read
Wrong-way risk
General: moves with the AI cycle. Nvidia owes the rent whatever happens to the party it assigns capacity to until an assignment is completed; the burden rises with weaker AI demand, and if an intended assignee weakens before taking the lease Nvidia keeps paying.

Research notes

At 2026-07-26 Nvidia's 10-Q split this commitment into data center leases not commenced of $25B (ev_10031) and a separate line, data center leases not commenced for third party, of $20B (ev_10037), with terms of about fifteen years that it expected to reassign to third parties (ev_190008); it warned that delays in completing assignments could leave it bearing the lease costs (ev_190009). The October disclosure gives one line of $74B, terms up to twenty years (ev_190006), commencement Q4 FY2027 to FY2033 (ev_190007), and says Nvidia may assign some of these leases to third parties (ev_190005); it no longer splits own use from third party. Related: the SB Energy PORTS-Pike guaranties (rel_openai_gu_2026) are guarantees of OpenAI's leases, not Nvidia's own leases, and are not part of this line (analysis).

Circular flows

Where Nvidia money goes out and comes back as demand for Nvidia systems. No loop has a disclosed dollar value on its return leg, so no circularity ratio can be computed.

PORTS-Pike: Nvidia stands behind OpenAI's rent on a campus that must run Nvidia systems

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia buys SB Energy stock and guarantees the landlord against an OpenAI rent default. Once buildings are ready, OpenAI will pay rent to SB Energy, and the site must deploy only Nvidia reference architecture. No rent, guaranty or system purchase is in effect yet.

  1. Nvidia to SB Energy: Prepaid forward for SB Energy Class N stock, funded; a further placement at the IPO is committed $1.5 billion (funded) Source (2)
  2. Nvidia to SB Energy: Residual value guaranties to the PORTS building landlords for leases of about 4.25 GW-IT to an OpenAI affiliate; paid only on tenant insolvency or uncured monetary default; not in force until a building is ready for service, the first expected in Nvidia's fiscal 2029 $105 billion (cap) Source (6)
  3. OpenAI to SB Energy: Rent under 17 twenty-year leases of about 8.0 GW-IT, commencing 2028 to 2032; rent total not disclosed Source (2)
  4. OpenAI to Nvidia: Compensation to Nvidia for the guaranty under a separate letter agreement; amount not disclosed Source (2)
  5. OpenAI to Nvidia: The premises must exclusively deploy Nvidia reference architecture for at least 20 years; no purchase value disclosed Source (2)

Closing leg is sourced as a contractual obligation (site exclusivity), not as a dollar amount. A ratio needs OpenAI's or SB Energy's disclosed spending on Nvidia systems for PORTS-Pike; neither side discloses it, so the ratio is not computable. The guaranty is contingent, not paid (no payments to date, ev_30023).

OpenAI: Nvidia equity in, Nvidia-based compute contracts out

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia commits equity to OpenAI's funding round, and OpenAI pairs the investment with dedicated Vera Rubin capacity and contracts with clouds that run Nvidia GPUs. CoreWeave, one of those clouds, runs only Nvidia GPUs, so part of the round can return to Nvidia as hardware sales; no amount is disclosed.

  1. Nvidia to OpenAI: Investment in OpenAI's 2026 round, disclosed by OpenAI; funded amount and schedule not disclosed $30 billion (committed) Source (3)
  2. OpenAI to Nvidia: 3 GW of dedicated inference and 2 GW of training on Vera Rubin, paired with the investment; no dollar value Source
  3. OpenAI to CoreWeave: OpenAI master services agreement with CoreWeave of March 2025, signed before the 2026 round, up to about this amount through October 2030 $11.9 billion (up to (contract signed March 2025, before the round)) Source
  4. CoreWeave to Nvidia: All GPUs in CoreWeave's fleet are Nvidia GPUs; Nvidia was 17% of CoreWeave's 2025 supplier purchases, dollar value not stated Source (2)

Nvidia's side is sourced only from OpenAI (Nvidia does not name the investment). OpenAI's spending on Nvidia hardware is not disclosed in dollars; the Vera Rubin capacity has no value, and Microsoft's Azure contract does not name Nvidia hardware as use of proceeds, so it does not count under spec/05. Ratio not computable. OpenAI's $250 billion Azure contract (ev_120111, 2025-10-29) predates the February 2026 round, so it is no longer drawn as a leg of this loop.

Anthropic: Nvidia stock purchase, then Nvidia GPU capacity from Nvidia-backed clouds

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia buys Anthropic stock in the IPO placement, and Anthropic has agreed to spend on Nvidia GPU compute at SpaceX, Nscale and Lambda. SpaceX and Nscale are Nvidia customers or buy Nvidia GPUs; Lambda's purchases are not on file. Nvidia also holds equity in SpaceX, Nscale and Lambda, so money leaves Nvidia once and can return through several paths.

  1. Nvidia to Anthropic: 120,481,927 Class N shares bought in the IPO concurrent private placement, closed 2026-11-20 $10 billion (funded) Source (2)
  2. Anthropic to SpaceX: SpaceXAI arrangements for Nvidia GPU compute into 2029, cancellable on 90 days notice after initial periods $120.5 billion (up to (contract)) Source (2)
  3. Anthropic to Nscale: Nscale GPU services agreements for Nvidia GPU compute into 2033; Nscale has no binding financing yet $44.6 billion (up to (contract)) Source (2)
  4. Anthropic to Lambda: Lambda agreements for Nvidia GPU compute into 2034; the August 2026 agreement is terminable $41.3 billion (contract value) Source (2)
  5. SpaceX to Nvidia: SpaceXAI deploys Nvidia Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin systems; no value disclosed Source (2)
  6. Nscale to Nvidia: Nvidia is Nscale's primary GPU manufacturer, bought through OEMs; no value tied to the Anthropic contract Source (2)

Nvidia's funded side is sourced (Anthropic 424B4). The return side is sourced only as supplier relationships without dollar values; none of the three clouds discloses Nvidia hardware bought for Anthropic. Ratio not computable. Nvidia's portion of Anthropic's Series G is not disclosed (rel_anthropic_eqc_2025).

CoreWeave: shareholder, supplier, renter and buyer of unsold capacity

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia owns CoreWeave stock, is the maker of every GPU in its fleet, rents compute from it and has agreed to buy capacity CoreWeave cannot sell to its own customers. Money flows to CoreWeave as equity and rent and flows back to Nvidia as GPU purchases, whose dollar value CoreWeave does not disclose.

  1. Nvidia to CoreWeave: 22,935,780 Class A shares at $87.20, January 2026 (earlier holding cost not disclosed) $2 billion (funded) Source (2)
  2. Nvidia to CoreWeave: Payments under the 2023 master services agreement: about $320 million to end 2024, $326.3 million in 2025, $59.6 million in Q1 2026 (sum $705.9 million, analysis) Source (3)
  3. Nvidia to CoreWeave: Order to buy CoreWeave's residual unsold capacity through 2032-04-13, initial value of the order form, not a cap; ends after a 90 day insolvency $6.3 billion (initial value (headline)) Source (3)
  4. CoreWeave to Nvidia: All GPUs are Nvidia GPUs; Nvidia was 17% of 2025 supplier purchases; dollar value not disclosed Source (2)

Round trip can be shown side by side only partly: Nvidia's rent paid is sourced ($705.9 million in components) but CoreWeave gives Nvidia's share of purchases (17%) without a dollar figure, and its $7.4 billion of OEM financing names no OEM (ev_20090). Ratio not computable without CoreWeave's dollar purchases from Nvidia.

Nscale: shareholder, noteholder, lease guarantor and customer

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia holds Nscale preferred shares and convertible notes, guarantees its Ward County lease and rents reserved GPU capacity from it. Nscale buys Nvidia GPUs through OEMs to build that capacity, so Nvidia's cash and credit can come back as hardware demand; no amount is disclosed.

  1. Nvidia to Nscale: Series B, SAFE converted to Series C-3, and Series C-4 preferred shares $1.18 billion (funded) Source (3)
  2. Nvidia to Nscale: 2028 convertible loan notes subscribed; a further $1.0 billion NVIDIA Sale is committed, closing not confirmed $1 billion (funded) Source (2)
  3. Nvidia to Nscale: Guarantee of Nscale's Ward County, Texas lease for its first five years, against a $470.0 million escrow and warrants $860.3 million (cap) Source (3)
  4. Nvidia to Nscale: NVIDIA master cloud services agreement for reserved GPU cluster capacity in Iceland, the UK and Norway $1.2 billion (contract value) Source (2)
  5. Nscale to Nvidia: Nvidia is the primary manufacturer of Nscale's GPUs, bought through third-party OEMs; no dollar value Source (2)

Nvidia's side is sourced from Nscale's S-1/A only (Nvidia names neither the stake nor the notes; the guarantee appears anonymously at $860 million). Nscale's purchases go through OEMs, which count under spec/05 only where a filing names Nvidia hardware; the S-1/A names Nvidia as primary GPU manufacturer but gives no dollar value. Ratio not computable.

IREN: Nvidia cloud contract and share rights booked into GPU cost

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia signed a five-year cloud services contract with IREN and received a right to buy IREN shares. IREN buys GPUs from Nvidia and booked the value of Nvidia's share rights as part of the cost of those GPUs, so part of the GPU price is paid in IREN equity options.

  1. Nvidia to IREN: Five-year cloud services contract under which Nvidia is IREN's customer $3.4 billion (contract value) Source (3)
  2. IREN to Nvidia: Right for Nvidia to buy up to 30 million IREN shares at $70, vesting with delivery of up to 600,000 GPUs; not exercised as reported $2.1 billion (headline (option, up to)) Source (3)
  3. IREN to Nvidia: GPUs acquired from Nvidia; the rights' fair value of about $793.4 million was capitalised into their cost (dollar value of the GPU purchase not stated) Source (2)

Nvidia's payments under the contract are not disclosed (only total contract value). IREN's GPU purchases from Nvidia have no stated dollar total; the $793.4 million fair value is a component of cost, not the purchase price. Ratio not computable; a round trip needs IREN's disclosed Nvidia purchases and Nvidia's payments in the same window.

NAVER: Nvidia equity tied to a Brookfield GPU vehicle that NAVER guarantees

Open at the closing leg · Analysis

Nvidia's investment in NAVER was conditional on NAVER securing project financing, which it met with a Brookfield vehicle that will buy GPUs and data centers. NAVER guarantees its cloud unit's usage fees to the vehicle, and the expansion is an Nvidia DSX AI factory, so Nvidia's equity helped trigger financing for a site Nvidia describes as its own AI factory design; no source says whose GPUs the vehicle buys.

  1. Nvidia to NAVER: Private placement of new NAVER shares; precondition met 2026-10-27, closing pending $1 billion (committed) Source (3)
  2. Brookfield to NAVER: Brookfield vehicle to invest in GPUs and data centers and provide computing power to NAVER Cloud; GPU vendor not named in the NAVER release $9 billion (up to (vehicle investment; vendor not named)) Source
  3. NAVER to Brookfield: NAVER guarantees NAVER Cloud's usage fees to the vehicle for up to eight years Source
  4. Nvidia to Brookfield: Nvidia is a strategic limited partner in Brookfield's AI infrastructure fund; amount not disclosed; link to the NAVER vehicle not stated Source (2)

Open at the closing leg: the Nvidia release describes the site as an Nvidia DSX AI factory, but no allowed source states that the Brookfield vehicle's GPUs are bought from Nvidia or their value. Needs the vehicle's purchase terms. Nvidia's $1 billion is not yet funded.

SharonAI: Nvidia minimum revenue on capacity SharonAI buys Nvidia hardware to build

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia agreed to pay SharonAI minimum revenue for reserved capacity it uses only when third parties do not buy it, with a revenue share. SharonAI committed to buy computing hardware for that capacity, so Nvidia's promise supports demand for its own GPUs.

  1. Nvidia to SharonAI: Master Cloud Services Agreement: minimum revenue subject to third-party utilisation; the 8-K says up to $4.88 billion, the 10-Q says no fixed aggregate value $4.88 billion (headline (up to)) Source (4)
  2. SharonAI to Nvidia: Commitment of about $4 billion for hardware and infrastructure in connection with the Nvidia agreement; Nvidia GPUs named in the collateral note, vendor split not stated Source (2)

Both sides are sourced only by SharonAI. Nvidia's committed amount and payments are not disclosed (headline only). The hardware commitment is about $4 billion but the share paid to Nvidia is not stated, so the ratio is not computable. SharonAI says it must keep access to additional financing (ev_80010).

Firmus: Nvidia equity and credit support for an Nvidia-only campus

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia is named in three Firmus equity rounds, one of them subject to closing, and gives the Batam campus revenue-sharing and credit support. The campus is a dedicated Nvidia DSX AI factory, so Nvidia's equity and support can return as system sales; no amount is disclosed.

  1. Nvidia to Firmus: Participation in the $505 million round (subject to closing) and follow-on in the $2 billion round; Nvidia amounts not disclosed Source (2)
  2. Nvidia to Firmus: Revenue-sharing and credit-support model for the Batam campus through 2034; size, form and trigger not disclosed Source (2)
  3. Firmus to Nvidia: Dedicated 360 MW Nvidia DSX AI factory campus, up to 170,000 accelerators; no value Source

No dollar amount on either side is disclosed. Needs Nvidia's investment amounts and Firmus's purchases from Nvidia. One news report, unconfirmed, says Firmus withdrew its listing application (ev_110048).

Nebius: Nvidia warrant money in, sole-supplier GPU purchases back

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia paid for a pre-funded warrant over Nebius shares, and Nebius says it relies on Nvidia for the GPU chips it uses. The loop closes through hardware purchases, but no Nvidia rental, backstop or guarantee was found.

  1. Nvidia to Nebius: Pre-funded warrant over 21,065,936 Class A shares $2 billion (funded) Source (2)
  2. Nebius to Nvidia: Nebius relies on Nvidia for the GPU chips it uses; purchase value not disclosed Source

Nvidia's side is reconciled on both sides. Nebius does not disclose its Nvidia purchases, so the ratio is not computable.

SpaceX: Nvidia holds SpaceX shares partly from xAI stakes, and SpaceX buys Nvidia systems

Closed loop · Analysis

Nvidia holds SpaceX shares that came at least partly from xAI stakes when SpaceX acquired xAI; their cost is not disclosed. SpaceX's AI unit is an Nvidia customer, finances its GPUs through lessors with no Nvidia money found, and sells the capacity to Anthropic, another Nvidia investee.

  1. Nvidia to SpaceX: SpaceX Class A shares held by Nvidia, at least partly from xAI holdings including the Series E; cost not disclosed Source (3)
  2. Valor to SpaceX: Valor leases computing equipment to xAI subsidiaries; recorded by SpaceX as failed sale-leaseback debt $12.9 billion (debt recorded) Source (2)
  3. Anthropic to SpaceX: Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 for about 325,000 Nvidia GPUs at Colossus Source
  4. SpaceX to Nvidia: SpaceXAI deploys Nvidia Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin systems; no value Source (2)

Nvidia's money in is not sourced as a cost (only market value). SpaceX's Nvidia purchases have no value. Seed A3's Nvidia stake in a GPU vehicle is unconfirmed (single Bloomberg report). Ratio not computable.

Is Nvidia a central bank?

Liquidity provision

Equity into buyers of Nvidia systems.

Partly supported

Investees pair Nvidia money with Nvidia compute; co-investors paid the same terms.

For

  • Nvidia bought $10.0 billion of Anthropic stock; Anthropic rents Nvidia GPUs from three clouds. Source (4)
  • Nscale took Nvidia equity and notes while relying on uncommitted financing. Source (3)

Against

  • Google bought identical Anthropic shares on the same terms. Source
  • Nvidia's Intel stake came with a product deal but no disclosed purchase commitment. Source (2)

Collateral support

Guaranties that make GPU debt bankable.

Partly supported

Borrowers and a landlord's noteholders cite Nvidia support; CoreWeave's lenders do not.

For

  • SB Energy says PORTS-Pike's financeability depends in significant part on Nvidia's guaranty; OpenAI is not investment grade. Source (3)
  • Galaxy's CoreWeave-tenanted notes cite Nvidia's capacity order and stake. Source (2)
  • Nvidia says some customers outgrow their credit, and it acted in response. Source (2)

Against

  • No CoreWeave credit agreement read names the order. Source (3)
  • PORTS-Pike has no debt yet. Source

Pricing of money

Nvidia's entry sets borrowing costs.

Not testable

No source ties a round price or loan spread to Nvidia.

For

    Against

    • Others led: GIC and Coatue at Anthropic, ASML at Mistral. Source (2)

    Lender of last resort

    Nvidia rescues firms others will not fund.

    Not supported

    No rescue deal is sourced; two backed firms rely on uncommitted financing.

    For

    • SharonAI says it needs further financing; Nvidia pays minimum revenue on its unsold capacity. Source (2)

    Against

    • Nvidia can end the CoreWeave order after a 90 day insolvency. Source
    • Intel raised $23.0 billion of equity; Anthropic held $95.6 billion of cash. Source (2)

    Where the analogy breaks

    Nvidia cannot create money. Its guarantees reach a $118.0 billion maximum against $266.7 billion of shareholders' equity at 25 October 2026; the OpenAI guaranty alone is $105 billion, recoverable only from OpenAI. Its support depends on the same AI demand. Sources (5)

    Nvidia gives equity and credit support to its buyers from a finite balance sheet; price setting and rescue are not shown.

    Analysis The verdicts are judgments on the evidence shown, not facts reported by any company.

    How the data was gathered

    Every relationship starts from what Nvidia was legally required to disclose: its annual and quarterly reports, current reports, holdings reports and ownership filings since January 2023. Then the same deal was traced in what the other company filed: its annual and quarterly reports, prospectuses, credit agreements and indentures, newest first. Company releases fill deals that never reached a filing. A sweep of every company's filings for Nvidia near words such as backstop, guarantee, warrant and lease found the rest.

    Pages from the named news publications could not be read when this register was compiled, so almost every figure rests on filings and company releases. Reported figures that could not be read are listed as needing a quote and are not shown. The register holds 1,295 citations: 1,289 primary and 6 from news. 53 of 80 relationships are disclosed by one side only.

    Source policy

    A figure is shown only if a primary source (a filing, the company's own release, a regulator, a court, a lien registry or a rating agency's public release) or two independent named publications (Bloomberg, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, the Financial Times, The Information, CNBC, Barron's, The Economist, Nikkei Asia, Axios) contain it. Otherwise it reads "Not confirmed". Blogs, social posts, aggregators and sell-side notes are never used. Every quote was found word for word in a saved copy of its source, and every number sits in or beside that quote.

    Definitions

    Funded
    Cash Nvidia has paid. On the page it counts the cost of shares still held: a stake partly sold counts only the part still reported.
    Committed
    A legally binding amount under a definitive agreement. Where no source says how much has been paid, it is counted once and never called unpaid.
    Contingent maximum
    The most Nvidia could be required to pay under a guarantee, backstop or similar promise, with the trigger stated. A guaranty that cannot yet be called is labeled not yet in force.
    Headline
    The largest figure announced, often "up to". Shown, never added to exposure.
    Gross exposure
    Funded plus committed plus contingent maximum, using confirmed amounts only. If any part is not disclosed it is a lower bound and reads "at least".
    Capacity backstop
    A promise to buy computing capacity that a cloud provider cannot sell to anyone else.
    Residual value guarantee
    A promise to cover the gap between an asset's guaranteed value and what it fetches when a lease ends or fails.
    Wrong-way risk
    Specific: Nvidia's exposure grows as the other company weakens. General: both move with AI demand. None: neither.
    Both sides
    Reconciled: both companies describe the deal the same way. Partly: they agree it exists but differ on terms. One side only: the other company has said nothing. Contradicted: they disagree on whether it exists or binds.
    Exposure at default
    Funded plus committed not yet paid plus the contingent maximum times a draw rate. The worst case draws everything; the base case is "not estimated" unless the draw is sourced. Loss is exposure less what Nvidia would receive or recover. Analysis

    Significance score

    score = 40 x gross exposure percentile + 25 x contingent share of gross + 15 x circularity percentile + 10 x counterparty weakness + 10 x lender reliance. Each part runs from 0 to 1. A part that cannot be computed scores 0.5, so an opaque private company is not ranked as the safest. Weakness comes from the indicators shown in each credit read, never from a letter grade. Analysis

    Staying current

    Watchers check Nvidia's filings every two hours on weekdays, every counterparty's filings every four hours, holdings and ownership filings daily, and named publications twice a day. Anything new goes to a review queue; nothing reaches this page until a person approves it. An amount of $1 billion or more, or any letter of intent, is re-verified every 30 days; other definitive deals every 90 days; completed or ended deals every year. Past its limit an amount shows "Not re-verified since" its date.

    This page describes financial exposure from public sources. It does not recommend buying or selling any security. Figures can be wrong or out of date; every one links to its source so you can check it.
